title: Bessent expects US-China AI incident channel as Washington leans on voluntary oversight
source_used: The Next Web (relaying Axios and Bloomberg); Digitimes opening lines
key_facts: Digitimes: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Washington and Beijing are likely to agree on a way to alert each other when AI goes wrong.
The Next Web, citing Axios: the US plans to propose a system for warning China about serious AI incidents, to help both governments act before a problem spreads.
Bessent discussed AI risks with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in New York in September, including rogue AI agents and non-state use of AI for cyber or biological attacks.
In the same Axios interview Bessent said AI leaders who want regulation 'should slow down' and that risk management belongs to the labs.
Trump said last week he does not want an AI safety deal with China.
Bessent said Chinese models can be '80%, 90% as powerful' as US ones but come without guardrails.
quote_evidence: Even so, the US plans to propose a system for warning China about serious AI incidents, Axios reported.
Bessent discussed AI with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in New York in September.
That openness has limits. Trump said last week he does not want an AI safety deal with China.
why_it_matters_hint: A possible first US-China channel for AI accidents, set against a US stance of no new federal rules.
notes: Digitimes page was cut to its first lines; facts taken from Digitimes opening and The Next Web. Axios original not opened. Interview is from 3 Oct, so not new today; the follow-up is Digitimes' 5 Oct framing.
